questions.question: Which of the following groups represents essential amino acid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Histidine, isoleucine,leucine,lysine**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The correct group representing essential amino acids is:**

 
 
• **Histidine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine**
 
 
 
• Essential amino acids are those that cannot be synthesized by the human body and must be obtained through diet.
 
• There are **nine essential amino acids:**
 
 
• Histidine
 
• Isoleucine
 
• Leucine
 
• Lysine
 
• Methionine
 
• Phenylalanine
 
• Threonine
 
• Tryptophan
 
• Valine
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alanine, arginine, asparagine, aspartic acid** – None of these are essential.

 
 
• While arginine is conditionally essential (for certain groups), the others are non-essential.
 
 
 
• **Alanine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine** – Alanine is not essential, though the others (isoleucine, leucine, lysine) are.
 
• **Glycine, proline, serine, tyrosine** – These are all non-essential amino acids.

questions.question: How many Mahajanapadas were there during the age of Buddha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**16**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the lifetime of Lord Gautam Buddha, 16 great powers (Mahajanpadas) existed in the 7th and early 6th centuries BC.
 
• These were Kasi, Kosala, Anga, Magadha, Vajji, Malla, Chedi, Vatsa, Kuru, Panchala, Machcha, Surasena, Assaka, Avanti, Gandhara and Kamboja.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Buddha was born in BC 563 in Lumbini (near the Indo-Nepal Border) and died at the age of eighty in BC 483 at Kushinagar in UP.
 
• At the age of 29, Gautama left home and rejected his life of riches and embraced a lifestyle of asceticism.
 
• After 49 consecutive days of meditation, Gautama attained enlightenment under a pipal tree (Bodhi Tree) at Bodhgaya a village in Bihar.
 
• Buddha gave his first sermon in the village of Sarnath in UP. This event is known as Dharma-Chakra-Pravartana.

 
• **Buddhist Councils marked important turning points in early Buddhism, In total, 4 major Buddhist councils were convened-** 

 
 
• The First Council was held soon after the Mahaparinirvan of the Buddha, around 483 BC in the Sattapani cave at Rajgriha. 
 
• The second Council was held in 383 BC in Vaishali.
 
• The third council was held in 250 BC in Patliputra.
 
• The fourth Council was held in 1st century AD at Kundalvana, Kashmir.

questions.question: Which inert gas is used in double-glazed windows to fill the space between the panes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Argon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Argon is a chemical element with the atomic number 18.

 
 
• It is a Nobel gas.
 
• It is in group 18 of the periodic table.
 
• Argon is the third most abundant gas in the Earth's atmosphere (0.094%)
 
• Uses: Fluorescent Lightning, Gas Discharge Tubes, Fluorescent Glow Starters.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Xenon

 
 
• Xenon(Xe) gas is also known as stranger gas.
 
• It is called 'STRANGER GAS' because the word 'XENON' means 'STRANGE' in Greek.
 
• The noble gas Xenon possesses the highest melting point.
 
• It was discovered by William Ramsay and Morris Travers in 1898.
 
• It is more than 4.5 times heavier than air.
 
• xenon is colorless, odorless, and tasteless.
 
• It is used in instruments for radiation detection.
 
 
 
• **Radon**
 
 
• Group 18 consists of six elements: helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon and radon.
 
• All these are gases and chemically unreactive.
 
• They form very few compounds.
 
• Because of this they are termed noble gases.
 
• All the noble gases except radon occur in the atmosphere.
 
• Xenon and radon are the rarest elements of the group.
 
• Radon is obtained as a decay product of 226Ra.
 
 
 
• **Helium**
 
 
• Helium is the 2nd most abundant element available in the universe. 
 
• Helium symbol (He) considered as noble gas having Atomic Number 2. 
 
• It is colorless, odourless, tasteless and non toxic.
 
• Helium gas is used to inflate party balloons, scientific balloons and blimps etc.
 
• Atomic mass of Helium is 4.002602 u.
 
• Boiling point of Helium is -268.9 °C.

questions.question: Which of the following is expressed as the total number of deaths per thousand population per year in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Death Rate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A mortality rate is the number of deaths during a particular period of time among a particular type or group of people.

 
 
• It is also called the Death Rate, that measured as the number of deaths per thousand persons in a year.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The number of newborn deaths per 1,000 live births is known as the infant mortality rate.
 
• The infant mortality rate is an essential indicator of a society's general health, in addition to providing crucial information regarding maternal and baby health.
 
• The crude mortality rate is derived by dividing the number of fatalities in a particular time by the number of people who were at risk of dying during that period.
 
• A death rate that is limited to a certain age group is known as an age-specific mortality rate.

questions.question: The entire salaries, allowances and pensions of the chairman and members of the Union Public Service Commission are charged on the ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Consolidated fund of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Consolidated Fund of India- 

 
 
• Consolidated Fund is constituted under Article 266 (1) of the Constitution of India.
 
• All expenditures of the government are incurred by this fund.
 
• All revenues received by the Centre by way of taxes (Income Tax, Central Excise, Customs, and other receipts) and all non-tax revenues in connection with the conduct of Government business are credited into the Consolidated Fund.
 
• All loans raised by the Government by the issue of Public notifications, treasury bills (internal debt), and loans obtained from foreign governments and international institutions (external debt) are credited into this fund.
 
• No amount can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund without authorization from the Parliament.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Contingency fund of India​**

 
 
• The Contingency Fund of India established under Article 267 (1) of the Constitution is the money maintained for a specific purpose which is placed at the disposal of the President to enable him/her to make advances to meet urgent unforeseen expenditure, pending authorization by the Parliament.
 
• It was added into the Indian Constitution through the Contingency Fund of India Act, 1950.
 
• Contingency fund refers to a fund that is set aside for emergencies and economic crisis.
 
 
 
• **Reserve Bank of India****​**
 
 
• RBI is known as the 'Central Bank of India' whose primary function to regulate the issue of Banknotes and keeping of reserves with a view to securing monetary stability in India and generally to operate the currency and credit system of the country.
 
• RBI is also known as 'Apex Bank of India'.
 
• RBI is also known as 'Banker's Bank'.

questions.question: Who was the founder of Jaipur-Atrauli gharana?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alladiya Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Jaipur Gharana :

 
 
• The Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana emerged from Alladiya Khan's family which originated from Atrauli and migrated to Jaipur.
 
• The Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana is Hindustani music founded by Alladiya Khan (1855–1946) in the late-19th century.
 
• The Gharana is known for its distinctive vocal aesthetics, raga repertoire, and technical aptitude.
 
• The chief exponents of the Jaipur Gharana are Alladiya Khan, Mallikarjun Mansur, Kesarbhai Kerkar, Kishori Amonkar, Shruti Sadolikar, Padma Talwalkar and Ashwini Bhide Deshpande.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Some other important Gharana**

 
 
• Patiala Gharana :

 
 
• ‘Patiala Gharana’ is one of the Gharanas in Indian Classical Music, which was founded by Ustad Fateh Ali Khan, and also Ustad Ali Baksh.
 
• Patiala Gharana has both kinds of singing – ‘Thumri’ and ‘Khyal’.
 
• The most famous exponents of Patiala Gharana are Pakistani ghazal singer Gulam Ali, and also the contemporary singer Shafqat Amanat Ali.
 
• Both the Pakistani singers have also garnered enormous fame in India.
 
 
 
• Banaras Gharana :
 
 
• The Benaras Gharana evolved as a result of the great lilting style of khayal singing known by Thumri singers of Benaras and Gaya. 
 
• It was founded by Pt Gopal Mishra.
 
• The chief exponents of the Benaras Gharana are Rajan Mishra, Sajan Mishra, Girija Devi and others. 
 
 
 
• Maihar Gharana :
 
 
• The Maihar Gharana is a Gharana or school of Hindustani classical music, a style of Indian classical music originating in the northern parts of the Indian subcontinent.

questions.question: Which of the following cell organelles is involved in apoptosis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mitochondria**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Apoptosis**, or programmed cell death, is a controlled process by which cells undergo self-destruction.
 
• This is crucial for maintaining health by eliminating damaged or unnecessary cells.
 
• The **mitochondria** play a central role in the **intrinsic pathway of apoptosis**.
 
• They release **cytochrome c** into the cytosol, which then triggers the activation of caspases (proteins that execute apoptosis).
 
• Once **cytochrome c** is released, it forms a complex with other proteins to activate **caspase-9**, which initiates a cascade that leads to cell death.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Golgi Apparatus**

 
 
• The **Golgi apparatus is involved in modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins and lipids **for secretion or delivery to other parts of the cell.
 
• While the Golgi is not directly involved in apoptosis initiation, it can be affected during cell death, leading to fragmentation.
 
• **Some proteins from the Golgi may also play a role in regulating apoptosis indirectly.**
 
• It is **central to processes like the production of lysosomes **and glycosylation of proteins.
 
 
 
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)**
 
 
• The **ER is responsible for the synthesis of proteins (rough ER) and lipids (smooth ER), as well as detoxification processes.**
 
• The** ER plays a crucial role in the unfolded protein respons**e (UPR) and ER stress-induced apoptosis.
 
• When misfolded proteins accumulate, the ER stress can trigger apoptosis via signalling pathways involving proteins like CHOP and caspase-12.
 
• It** also stores calcium, and calcium release from the ER can amplify apoptotic signals.**
 
 
 
• **Lysosome**
 
 
• **​** **Lysosomes are responsible for breaking down waste materials and cellular debris using digestive enzymes.**
 
• While not directly initiating apoptosis, lysosomal enzymes like cathepsins can be released during apoptosis, contributing to the degradation of cellular components.
 
• **Lysosomes are involved in autophagy,** a process that can promote cell survival or death, depending on the context.

questions.question: ________ of the Indian Constitution sets qualifications for being a member of Lok Sabha.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 84**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 84** of the Indian Constitution sets the qualifications required for being a member of the **Lok Sabha** (the House of the People, the lower house of Parliament).
 
• Key qualifications under **Article 84** include:
 
 
• The individual must be a citizen of India.
 
• They must be at least **25 years old**.
 
• They must possess other qualifications as may be prescribed by law made by Parliament, including not holding an office of profit under the government and being of sound mind.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 74**:

 
 
• Deals with the **Council of Ministers** to aid and advise the President.
 
• There shall be a **Council of Ministers**, with the **Prime Minister** at its head, to **aid and advise the President**.
 
• The President **shall act in accordance with such advice**, except where the Constitution explicitly requires otherwise.
 
 
 
• **Article 64**:
 
 
• The **Vice President of India** acts as the **ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States)**.
 
• The Vice President assumes this role automatically upon being elected as Vice President.
 
• In case of a tie during voting, the Vice President, as Chairman, exercises a **casting vote** to break the deadlock.
 
 
 
• **Article 76**:
 
 
• Relates to the **Attorney-General of India**.
 
• The** Attorney General is appointed by the President **of India and must be qualified to be appointed a Judge of the Supreme Court.
 
• This means the person must be a citizen of India and must have been an advocate for at least 10 years, a judge of a high court for 5 years, or an eminent jurist.

questions.question: What is it called in basketball when a shot goes through the basket without touching the rim or backboard?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Swish**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In basketball, a **swish** refers to a shot that passes cleanly through the net without touching the **rim, backboard, or hoop**.
 
• It is considered one of the most accurate and perfect shots a player can make.
 
• The ball goes through the basket in a way that it doesn't make contact with the rim or backboard, producing a distinctive "swish" sound as it moves through the net.
 
• It's a** visually satisfying shot for both the player and spectators**, as it demonstrates precision, skill, and control.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Screen**:

 
 
• In basketball, a **screen** (also called a "pick") is a move where a player blocks or "screens" a defender to free up a teammate for a shot or pass.
 
 
 
• **Dime**:
 
 
• A **dime** is a slang term for an assist, where one player passes the ball to a teammate who scores immediately.
 
 
 
• **Technical Foul**:
 
 
• A **technical foul** is a penalty given for unsportsmanlike conduct or violations unrelated to physical play (e.g., arguing with the referee).

questions.question: When was the preamble to the Indian Constitution amended?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 1976**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Preamble of the Constitution was amended by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act.
 
• The Preamble of the Constitution was amended only once and it was in 1976.
 
• The Forty-second Amendment(42nd) of the constitution is also known as the "Mini Constitution".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• This made drastic changes in the constitution:
 
 
• Changed the description of India from a "sovereign democratic republic" to a "sovereign, socialist secular democratic republic".
 
• Changed the words "unity of the nation" to "unity and integrity of the nation".
 
• Added a list of ten fundamental duties by adding Part IV-A.
 
• Added part XIV-A.
 
• Increased the tenure of Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies from 5 years to 6, but it was canceled by 44thamendment act​
 
• Made the President bound by the advice of the cabinet.
 
 
 
• Amendment was passed during the Indira Gandhi government.
 
 
• Indira Gandhi constituted Swaran Singh Committee to study about amending the constitution in 1976.
 
• Recommendations of the Swaran Singh committee made several changes to the Constitution including the Preamble, through the Forty-second Amendment of the Constitution of India.
